name: particle-dissolve
title: Particle Dissolve
description: The frame breaks into drifting grey dust, bright parts throwing theirs furthest, with specks that twinkle and a little colour fringing; the next scene coalesces back out of the dust. Runs its WebGL shader over two built-in panels (a stat and a bar chart, then a render queue; text and colours from variables), not over the host's scenes: 60 frames of the first panel, a 36-frame transition, then the second panel. To use it between your own scenes, copy the shader into your composition and feed it your two frames as textures.
useWhen: A scene change should read as the picture breaking down into matter and reassembling, not one image fading through another.
The moment can afford well over a second; the dust needs time to form, drift and gather.
The outgoing scene has bright content worth watching disintegrate: highlights throw their dust furthest.
avoidWhen: You only need texture over a plain crossfade: use grain-dissolve.
You want an organic flowing break-up rather than a granular one: use perlin-dissolve.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Label
variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Value
variables.description: The big number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Bars
variables.description: Bar heights as percentages, separated by commas (up to 12); the last bar is highlighted.

variables.label: Title
variables.description: Small heading above the list in the sample scene.

variables.label: Rows
variables.description: Rows of the list as name | status, separated by semicolons (up to 5).
variables.default: intro-scene.mp4 | Done; feature-tour.mp4 | Rendering; pricing-outro.mp4 | Queued

variables.label: Particle size
variables.description: Size of one speck. Pixel sizes are for a 1280×720 frame and scale with the frame.

variables.label: Aberration
variables.description: Colour fringing on the drifting picture.

variables.label: Direction
variables.description: Where the dissolve starts: from the centre, or sweeping one way.

variables.label: Stagger
variables.description: How much the break-up is spread over the transition.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Specks are a few pixels; 0.75 is the floor for them.
